# Gaming Support

`customer_support.model.b2c.gaming` · vertical · parent `customer_support.model.b2c`

> Supporting players of live-service games. Volume is outage-shaped and calendar-shaped at the same time: launches, patches and timed events are known dates that produce order-of-magnitude surges, and unplanned downtime produces the same surge without the warning. What is specific to this vertical is what an outage costs — not access, but progress. A player who could not log in during a limited-time event did not lose an evening's entertainment, they lost progression they had earned, and the remediation is a compensation decision applied to a population rather than an apology written to a person. A second, larger part of the queue is adversarial by construction. Account theft, chargebacks, ban appeals and item-restoration requests all involve a claimant whose account of events cannot be taken at face value, where the correct answer is frequently no, and where saying no consistently across millions of cases is the actual quality bar. This is the inverse of the service reflex every consumer support agent is trained on, and agents who cannot hold it get farmed. The audience is organised and instantaneous. A single inconsistent ruling is screenshotted, posted and compared against every other ruling within minutes, so consistency between agents matters more than the quality of any individual response. This branch reactivates account_relationship_management, which B2C switches off. In a game with a heavy-spend tail, the top accounts genuinely are named accounts with dedicated handling, and the capability's object graph has a real referent here that it does not have in streaming or retail. The error carried in from streaming is treating an outage as purely a communications problem. The error carried in from ecommerce is reflexive goodwill: in a virtual economy, granting items to settle a complaint is inflation and it is permanent.


## Characteristics

|  |  |
|---|---|
| requester | a player, frequently young, usually contacting from a console or phone mid-session, and part of a community that will compare our answer with everyone else's |
| typical_resolution_hours | 8 |
| volume_shape | event-driven and violently spiky — launches, patches, timed events and downtime each produce multiples of baseline within minutes |
| staffing_model | pooled agents with specialist pods for account security, payments/chargebacks and appeals, plus VIP handling for the heavy-spend tail |
| coverage | 24x7 — the playerbase is global and peak play is everyone else's night |
| automation_level | high on account, billing and known-issue intents; deliberately low on appeals, where an automated no is the most inflammatory possible output |
| notes | Compensation decisions are made once and applied to millions of accounts. They belong to incident command rather than to individual agents, and every attempt to devolve them has produced inconsistency that outlived the outage.  |

## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.ticket`

Requires `intent_ref`, `resolution_type`


> Intent has to separate the adversarial classes — appeal, chargeback, account recovery, item restoration — from ordinary service contacts at intake, because they need different evidence standards, different agents and a different default answer. Routing them into the general queue is how a bans queue becomes a refunds queue.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.incident`

Requires `is_customer_visible`, `affected_customer_count`, `closing_broadcast_sent`


> The closing broadcast is load-bearing here because the compensation decision usually rides on it. Players who miss it open tickets asking whether they were included, and that second wave is frequently larger than the first.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.customer_sentiment`

Requires `public_exposure`, `audience_widening`


> Audience widening in gaming is not one thread acquiring recipients; it is a ruling being posted to a forum where thousands of players evaluate it. The sentiment reading that matters is community-level, and an individual conversation can look calm while the aggregate is on fire.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.escalation`

Requires `origin`, `is_repeat_escalation`


> Repeat escalation is the signal that separates a genuine grievance from an appeal being re-rolled until an agent says yes. Both look identical in a single ticket and only the history tells them apart, which is why the history has to be on the object rather than in an agent's memory.
